schema.headline: Can You Teach English in Thailand With No Experience? (2026 Guide)

content:
Home›First teaching job

Local decision guide · Updated 3 October 2026

Can you teach English in Thailand with no experience?

If you have a bachelor’s degree but have never taught, the honest answer is: it can be possible to compete for some entry-level roles, but the degree alone does not secure a job, visa, work permit or teacher authorization.

Official rules separated from hiring examplesSalary evidence tied to a dated listing
Affiliate disclosure: This guide includes optional course referral links. SiamTEFL may earn a commission if you enrol; it does not change the price or our assessment. How this works.

The decision in one minute

You may be a viable entry-level applicant if: you have a completed bachelor’s degree, can document it in the form your employer and relevant authorities accept, meet the school’s language and safeguarding criteria, and a school is willing and able to sponsor the proper immigration, work-permit and teaching-authorization process.

No classroom experience is not an automatic disqualifier. A Bangkok vacancy posted 4 August 2026 lists no experience required, a bachelor’s degree required, 120+ TEFL hours required, and ฿32,000–37,000 per month. It is one four-month, five-vacancy listing with a stated 30 September deadline—not evidence of an average salary, an open vacancy today or your likelihood of being hired. Its details are not perfectly consistent about whether TEFL is required or advantageous, so confirm the condition with the employer.

Your first gate is eligibility and employer sponsorship, not the certificate. Before paying for a course or booking a flight, ask a named school what it needs from your nationality, degree and documents, and who handles work authorization.

Your route from eligibility to application

A decision path for your first teaching job

Can I teach in Thailand with no experience?Start with the gates that decide whether you can apply and work.
01

Bachelor’s degree?

Yes: check that the school and authorities accept your degree subject and documents.

No: pause before spending on TEFL or travel; many sponsored school routes require a degree. Ask the employer and authorities about your exact case.

02

Teaching experience?

No: target entry-level vacancies that explicitly accept new teachers and describe onboarding, lesson materials or classroom support.

03

TEFL?

Helpful; sometimes requested. One dated Bangkok listing asks for 120+ hours while accepting no experience. TEFL helps preparation and may meet an employer’s criterion; it does not replace work authorization or guarantee hiring.

04

What jobs should I target?

Start with private-school or language-centre vacancies that name the employer, accept new teachers, and explain sponsorship and classroom support. Verify contract length, paid months, duties and first-pay timing.

05

What should I do before applying?

Prepare degree and identity documents, check the vacancy’s certificate rules, request the visa/work-permit and teacher-permission process in writing, and make a cash runway for a delayed first salary.

What “qualified” means in practice

Four different questions are often compressed into one: Can you be hired? Can you lawfully work? Can you meet teaching-profession rules for the school? Does a particular employer want your profile? They have different decision-makers.

GateWhat sources establishWhat you must confirm
DegreeThe Ministry of Labour says a foreign worker needs an eligible temporary stay status, relevant ability and employer documents. Teachers’ Council temporary-permission material describes routes including a bachelor’s degree in a field needed by the institution.Whether your subject, issuing institution and authenticated documents meet the process for your employer and role.
Teacher authorizationBelow-university teaching is subject to Teachers’ Council requirements. Official materials describe temporary permission or waiver processes in applicable cases; a TEFL certificate is not a Thai teaching licence.Which permission or licence applies to your school, role and hiring term, and whether the school will submit it.
Immigration and workThe MFA’s Non-Immigrant B (Teaching) checklist calls for school acceptance, government-agency approval, education evidence, school documents and a résumé. Labour guidance excludes tourist/transit status from first-time work-permit eligibility.Which consular checklist applies where you apply, the sequence of visa and work-permit steps, and who files each item.
Employer fitVacancies set their own degree, English level, availability, age-group and certificate criteria. Listings are snapshots.Whether you meet the current criteria and the contract states salary, paid months, hours, duties, benefits and start date.

Practical rule: Do not teach on a tourist entry while waiting for paperwork or treat a recruiter’s reassurance as official permission. Have the school confirm the lawful sequence in writing; verify visa instructions with the Thai embassy/consulate handling your case and work requirements with the Department of Employment.

What a TEFL certificate can—and cannot—do

A reputable TEFL course can give you lesson-planning practice, classroom routines, feedback and a credential some employers request. The Bangkok listing above is one example of a role with a 120-hour criterion and no previous experience requirement.

TEFL does not substitute for a degree where one is required, a Thai teacher licence or waiver where applicable, a Non-Immigrant visa, a work permit, or a school’s hiring decision. “120 hours” alone does not ensure an employer accepts a given provider or online format. Ask target schools which certificates they recognize.

If you want face-to-face practice before your first class, compare the Bangkok course review and our online vs in-person guide. Course fees are a separate purchase decision from legal eligibility and job prospects.

Which first jobs make sense to target?

With a non-education bachelor’s degree and no classroom record, start with vacancies that explicitly accept new teachers and spell out their support. The current example is a young-learner placement that lists training, lesson plans and a Thai assistant teacher. That is an example of a more scaffolded first job, not proof of a general hiring pattern.

Private-school placements, language centres and agency-supported posts can differ in schedule, contract length, support and sponsorship. Verify the legal employer, workplace, paid months, teaching hours, non-teaching duties, probation, holiday pay and who files work and teacher-permission documents.

Do not assume a short TEFL certificate qualifies you for a licensed-teacher position at an international school. Check that employer’s actual qualification and experience criteria.

What salary is realistic to plan around?

Use vacancies as examples, not a national pay scale. The cited Bangkok listing advertised ฿32,000–37,000 monthly, no accommodation (assistance offered), and a four-month contract. Ask whether every month is paid, how school breaks are handled and when the first salary arrives.

We do not have a representative 2026 dataset for one reliable starting salary across Thailand. Location, employer, nationality criteria, degree, certificate, paid months, housing, hours and sponsorship terms change the offer. Budget against a written offer and actual housing costs—not the top of one advertisement.

Use the cash-runway calculator and Bangkok cost guide to model tuition, time until first pay, accommodation, food, transport, travel and a reserve. These use your inputs; they are not salary or cost-of-living promises.

Before you fly: get these answers in writing

  1. Job: named school and legal employer, workplace, start date, salary, paid months, hours, duties, probation and contract end date.
  2. Eligibility: degree subject and authentication, passport requirements, English criteria, background check and accepted TEFL format.
  3. Work authorization: visa category and application location, ministry approval, work-permit sequence, Teachers’ Council licence/temporary permission, responsible party and fees. Do not assume a tourist entry can be used to work.
  4. Money: deposit/refund terms, course balance, housing and deposit, flight, insurance, transport and buffer for delays or late first pay.
  5. Classroom support: age group, curriculum, materials, Thai co-teacher, orientation, observation and who helps after you start.
  6. Documents and timing: degree/transcripts, translations or authentication if required, passport validity, police certificate, medical paperwork and processing time.

Rules and consular procedures change. The official sources below are a starting point; your school and responsible authorities must confirm the current route for your case.

Should you take TEFL now—or wait?

Take TEFL before moving if…

  • Target schools explicitly require it or shortlist certified applicants.
  • You have never planned a lesson and want observed practice before your first class.
  • You want to apply from abroad with a stronger, concrete application.
  • You confirmed the format is accepted by employers you want.

Choose the lowest-cost route that meets actual employer criteria and gives the practice you value. Compare added support in our Standard vs All-In guide.

Wait before paying if…

  • You have not checked your degree and documents against role requirements.
  • You do not know whether the vacancy requires 120 hours, an awarding body or in-person practice.
  • Your chosen employer says TEFL is optional and explains onboarding and classroom support.
  • You need to confirm a compliant job and budget before committing to Bangkok.

Ask employers first. A certificate can prepare you, but buying one before understanding hiring and sponsorship can leave the central questions unanswered.

A sensible next move

Do not self-reject, and do not move on the strength of “Thailand needs teachers.” Identify several current entry-level vacancies, check their criteria, and ask each employer what it sponsors and which documents it needs. If TEFL is required or the classroom practice matters to you, choose a course after those checks. Keep a cash runway through a delayed first pay date.

Sources checked 3 October 2026: Thai MFA: Non-Immigrant B (Teaching) · Ministry of Labour: foreign worker eligibility and documents · Teachers’ Council: professional/temporary permit search · OPEC: temporary permit for foreign teachers · Bangkok vacancy TH59169, posted 4 Aug 2026.

General information, not legal advice or a hiring guarantee. Rules vary by school, role, nationality and application location. Recheck official instructions before travel or payment.

Considering in-person training in Bangkok?

Review the course, published fees and support terms, then verify eligibility directly with the provider and prospective employer.

schema.headline: How Much Can a First-Time English Teacher Earn in Thailand? (2026)

content:
Home›First teaching salary

Local decision guide · Checked 3 October 2026

How Much Can a First-Time English Teacher Earn in Thailand?

There is no single promised “new-teacher salary.” Compare real offers by role, school, eligibility, benefits and location—not a national average alone.

2026 listings separated from market-wide claimsOffer scenarios are not guarantees

The short answer

For a first English-teaching job in Thailand, think in terms of an offer range, not one promised “new-teacher salary.” A current 2026 Bangkok-area listing accepts candidates with no teaching experience and advertises ฿32,000–฿37,000 per month; it also asks for a degree and a 120-hour TEFL certificate. A separate 2026 recruitment listing describes ฿30,000–฿36,000 as typical for many of its roles. These are useful examples, not a census of all Thai jobs.

Use ฿35,000 as a planning scenario when comparing offers—not as a national average, legal minimum, or guaranteed starting rate. Some first-time teachers may find better offers, especially where the role, subject, school, qualifications, location, and benefits align. A higher number can also come with higher costs or more demanding eligibility.

Before deciding, compare written monthly pay with school type, weekly teaching and office hours, paid breaks, housing or transport support, insurance, visa and work-permit support, and the actual location. Salary alone does not tell you what you can save.

If you are still checking whether you can get hired with no classroom experience, read our first-job eligibility guide.

Why “average teacher salary” can mislead a first-time applicant

An average drawn from many listings can combine different school types, cities, subjects, experience levels, and benefit packages. A commercial provider’s placement figures describe the roles it fills; a job-board sample describes ads visible on that platform. Neither automatically predicts what one new applicant will be offered.

For example, a 2026 market guide from a TEFL provider separates public schools (฿25,000–฿45,000), private/bilingual schools (฿35,000–฿70,000), language centres (฿25,000–฿40,000 or hourly), and international schools (฿80,000–฿170,000+). The same page separately reports that its own private/bilingual placements start at ฿45,000–฿50,000. Those are different datasets and should not be collapsed into a single “beginner average.”

The useful question is: What kind of job could I qualify for, and what does this particular offer include?

A salary map: ฿30k to ฿50k

These five points are comparison scenarios, not official salary bands or statistical percentiles. Current job listings and provider ranges overlap, and actual eligibility varies.

Monthly gross payHow to read it as a new applicantWhat to check
฿30,000A lower planning case that appears in entry-level recruitment and school-market guidance.Is it gross or net? Are visa/work-permit costs covered? How many paid months are guaranteed?
฿35,000A practical midpoint for comparing a first offer; a 2026 no-experience listing advertises ฿32k–฿37k.Is the school outside central Bangkok? Are breaks, overtime, and the exact campus stated?
฿40,000A stronger offer in some school or location combinations, but not proof of a particular credential premium.Compare hours, duties, benefits, commute, and contract length with lower offers.
฿45,000A higher first-job scenario that may be possible in selected private/bilingual roles or where a candidate matches the role well.Is the figure from an actual job ad or a recruiter’s own placements? What qualifications are required?
฿50,000An ambitious scenario, not a safe baseline for every first-time teacher. Some provider-reported private/bilingual placements start in this vicinity.Check whether the role is specialist, subject-specific, or has extra duties; verify the offer in writing.

Three fictional offer scenarios

The people below are fictional teaching-candidate models created only to explain trade-offs. They are not real teachers, interviews, testimonials, or observed salary outcomes. Their salaries are hypothetical gross monthly amounts.

Alex: ฿35,000

Alex receives an offer at a school outside central Bangkok. Alex has a bachelor’s degree, a 120-hour TEFL certificate, and no classroom teaching experience. The offer looks close to the currently advertised no-experience range cited above. Alex checks commute time, paid school breaks, and whether the school will arrange the required immigration and teaching permissions before accepting.

Maya: ฿45,000

Maya receives an offer from a private/bilingual school. The higher amount is attractive, but Maya compares teaching and office hours, class sizes, housing support, and whether the role requires subject teaching or additional experience. The number alone does not establish that the school type caused a salary premium.

Chris: ฿50,000

Chris receives a hypothetical higher-end entry offer after matching a school’s subject and qualification requirements. Chris treats it as an individual offer, not the normal result of adding a TEFL certificate. Chris confirms the exact duties, probation terms, pay dates, and work authorization process in the contract.

What can change a starting offer?

School and role. Public, private/bilingual, language-centre, and international-school jobs are different markets. Specialized subject teaching can have different requirements from general English classes.

Qualifications and eligibility. A bachelor’s degree, education degree, teaching license, teaching certificate, or TEFL/TESOL training may be required by a particular employer or relevant process. Requirements vary by role and applicant. Thailand’s government guidance describes temporary, school-requested permission for certain foreign teachers without a professional license; it lists age and education/qualification conditions. This is not the same as a universal guarantee that any certificate makes someone eligible.

Experience and evidence of teaching skill. Classroom experience can strengthen an application, but employers decide how they value it. A TEFL course with observed practice can help someone prepare and demonstrate skills; the sources reviewed do not establish a guaranteed salary increase caused by TEFL alone.

Location, timing, and competition. A campus outside a major city, an urgent hiring window, or a hard-to-fill subject may change the available offer. These are plausible offer factors, not a quantified causal formula.

The whole contract. Compare monthly gross salary, paid months, probation, paid holidays, teaching and office hours, overtime, housing, insurance, visa/work-permit support, and deductions. Ask for each item in writing.

Can you live on ฿35,000 in Bangkok?

Possibly, but the answer depends heavily on rent, commute, lifestyle, and deductions. As a rough current reference, Numbeo’s Bangkok page (community-reported prices; last updated 2 October 2026) lists a one-bedroom apartment at about ฿11,650 outside the city centre and ฿22,742 in the centre. Those are citywide reference figures, not a promise about a specific apartment or a complete personal budget.

At a ฿35,000 gross salary, central rent alone could take a large share of pay. Shared housing, a lower-cost neighbourhood, or a provincial location may change the budget substantially. Taxes, deposits, utilities, transport, and unpaid breaks also matter. Do not assume that gross pay equals take-home pay or that a first salary arrives immediately after arrival.

Next topic: Can You Live in Bangkok on a ฿35,000 Teaching Salary? (S003 planned) — this follow-up is not published yet.

Should you get a TEFL certificate?

Treat TEFL as a preparation and eligibility question, not a guaranteed pay-rise investment. Some vacancies require a TEFL certificate: the cited 2026 no-experience Bangkok-area listing requires 120+ hours. Other employers may set different requirements. A certificate with practical teaching experience can help you prepare for lesson planning and classroom management, but it does not replace checking the employer’s degree, licensing, visa, and work-permit requirements.

Before paying for a course, compare course hours, assessed teaching practice, accreditation/awarding body, total cost, refund terms, and the jobs you actually plan to apply for. Ask recruiters whether a credential is required for the specific vacancy and whether any advertised placement or salary figure refers to their own graduates only.

What should you target for a first job?

Set a minimum acceptable total package, then target roles where your qualifications match. A first role can be valuable if it provides legal employment, dependable pay, a manageable commute, clear hours, and real classroom experience. Do not accept vague promises of later salary increases in place of written terms.

Use this checklist before signing:

  • Monthly gross salary, pay date, probation rate, and any deductions
  • Teaching hours, office hours, class sizes, and additional duties
  • Paid holidays and whether salary continues during school breaks
  • Housing, insurance, transport, and overtime terms
  • Who arranges and pays for the visa, work permit, and required teaching permission
  • Contract length, notice period, and what happens if the school placement changes
  • Campus location and a realistic monthly housing/commute budget

Your next decision

First estimate what a specific offer leaves after housing and essential costs. Then decide whether the role is a good first-year step and whether extra training is worth its cost for the jobs you want.

Salary figures are volatile. Job-board listings and provider market guides are not official wage statistics. The scenarios above are illustrative only. This guide is general information, not legal advice or a promise of employment or salary. Requirements vary; confirm your case with the school and responsible authorities.

Sources checked 3 October 2026: The TEFL Org: Bangkok-area vacancy TH59169 · TEFL.com: 2026 Thailand listing · Essential TEFL: Thailand salary guide and placement claims · Thailand.go.th: temporary teaching permission overview · Thai MFA: Non-Immigrant Visa B · Numbeo: Bangkok cost-of-living data.

Recheck current listings and official visa, work-permit and teacher-permission procedures before making a decision.

content:
Home›Provider review

Independent provider review · Updated 1 October 2026

Essential TEFL Bangkok: an independent review

A practical look at the course choices, published fees and employment support—so you can decide what to ask before committing.

Official pages checked 1 Oct 2026Referral relationship disclosed
Affiliate disclosure: SiamTEFL may earn a commission if you enrol through links on this page. It does not change your price or our assessment. How this works.

Quick take

Essential TEFL offers face-to-face training at a Bangkok centre, with a practical 120-hour course, a separate 168-hour TQUK Level 5 route, a paid internship and an All-In bundle. The published course comparison lists fees of ฿45,000, ฿50,000, ฿90,000 and ฿130,000 respectively. This is a four-week, in-person format for the main courses, with real classroom practice described on the provider site.

It may fit someone who specifically wants in-person training in Bangkok and values local guidance. Whether the higher-support options justify their price depends on your eligibility, housing needs and what the placement terms mean for your situation.

Important employment distinction: the provider’s current comparison says eligible native English speakers with a bachelor’s degree receive guaranteed interviews; the school makes the hiring decision. Do not read interview or placement support as guaranteed employment.

Published course options

RoutePublished feeWhat the course page describesHousing
Standard TEFL฿45,000120 hours, in-person practical trainingNot included
TQUK Level 5฿50,000168 guided learning hours, assignments, regulated qualificationNot included
Paid internship฿90,000Training plus paid teaching placement; eligibility appliesConfirm terms
All-In bundle฿130,000120-hour course, first-month accommodation, visa guidance, orientation and 12-month supportFirst month included

Prices and descriptions as displayed on the official course comparison on 1 October 2026. Fees, dates and package terms can change; confirm directly before paying.

What looks useful

  • Observed classroom practice: the provider describes teaching practice with Thai students and trainer feedback.
  • Clear course distinction: Standard is described as practical training; Level 5 adds assignments and a regulated qualification. Check which qualification employers you care about actually require.
  • Bangkok-based context: the school is near Lat Phrao MRT, useful if you want to train in the city rather than online.
  • Optional support tiers: the All-In listing spells out first-month housing, visa document guidance, orientation and year-long career support.

What to check before booking

  1. Ask what “placement,” “guaranteed interview,” or “paid internship” means for your passport, degree, English level and experience. Request the eligibility and refund terms in writing.
  2. Confirm the awarding body and exact certificate for your chosen route. The provider lists Standard as 120 hours and TQUK Level 5 as 168 guided learning hours.
  3. For All-In, confirm the accommodation location, start/end dates, what happens after month one and any conditions attached to support.
  4. Ask about the deposit, balance due date, cancellations, date changes, taxes and payment fees.
  5. Check whether your own immigration and work-permit circumstances allow the role you have in mind. A course provider cannot determine your legal eligibility for you.

Who might this suit?

Potentially a fit: you want a hands-on Bangkok course, can attend four weeks in person and are comparing the total move budget rather than tuition alone.

Look carefully at alternatives: you need a fully online qualification, already hold a qualification employers require, need employment guaranteed regardless of eligibility, or cannot travel to Bangkok. Compare independent course providers and ask prospective employers which qualification they accept.

Independent evidence and limitations

This review evaluates published course descriptions and terms, not observed teaching quality or a verified graduate outcome dataset. Provider pages are primary sources for current prices and package descriptions, but they are marketing material. We do not treat testimonials as representative outcome evidence or claim to have independently audited placements.

We found differences in wording across provider pages around hours, placement and support. This page uses the current course comparison as the primary fee reference and paraphrases employment support conservatively. Ask the provider to confirm your exact course and eligibility in writing.

Sources: Courses and fees · Dates and fees · All-In bundle terms. Accessed 1 October 2026.

Verdict

Essential TEFL has a legible Bangkok-based offer with multiple training and support tiers. The strongest reason to consider it is the in-person classroom practice plus local orientation. The main decision risk is assuming that job support guarantees a job, or that an advertised package resolves every visa or housing need. Verify those details against your own circumstances before enrolling.

content:
Home›Course comparison

A decision guide · Updated 1 October 2026

Standard vs All-In: what does ฿85,000 more buy?

Same Bangkok provider, very different amount of help bundled around the course. Here is a neutral way to compare the ฿45,000 and ฿130,000 routes.

Affiliate disclosure: This page contains a referral link. A commission may be paid if you enrol; it does not change the price or our decision framework. Details.

The short answer

The All-In bundle costs ฿85,000 more than Standard on the published course comparison. That difference buys first-month accommodation, visa document guidance, Bangkok orientation and extended career support, alongside the 120-hour course. Eligible native English speakers with a bachelor’s degree receive guaranteed interviews according to the provider; the school makes the hiring decision.

Whether the difference is worthwhile depends on your real alternative costs and how much you value a local team helping coordinate the first month. It is not automatically a saving: compare the bundle inclusions with quotes and support you would actually use.

Course only

Standard TEFL

฿45,000 listed course fee
  • 120-hour in-person course
  • Observed classroom practice
  • Job support terms depend on eligibility
  • Accommodation not included
  • Flight and living expenses separate
More included support

All-In bundle

฿130,000 listed bundle fee
  • 120-hour in-person course
  • First month accommodation
  • Visa document guidance
  • Bangkok orientation
  • 12-month career support

Published prices and package inclusions: official course comparison and All-In detail page, checked 1 October 2026.

What the extra ฿85,000 covers

ItemStandardAll-InYour question
120-hour Bangkok courseIncludedIncludedDoes this fit your qualification goal?
First month accommodationNot includedListed as includedWhat exact room, location and dates?
Visa documentsGuidance listedFull document support listedWhich visa process and what remains your responsibility?
Employment supportPlacement support12-month career support; guaranteed interviews for eligible candidatesDo you qualify? What outcomes are actually guaranteed?
OrientationNot listed as includedBangkok orientation listedWould you otherwise buy or arrange this?
Employment itselfNot guaranteedSchool makes final decisionInterview guarantee is not an employment guarantee.

“Included” describes the provider’s published bundle. It is not a value estimate. Ask what is covered in the contract and what happens if the placement or arrival timing changes.

When Standard may make more sense

  • You already live in Bangkok or have a reliable place to stay.
  • You can organise your own arrival logistics and have a contingency fund.
  • You want the in-person course and do not need the bundle’s added support.
  • You want to compare different providers’ course-only prices and job assistance.

When All-In may be worth exploring

  • You are moving from abroad and value having first-month housing arranged.
  • You meet the provider’s stated eligibility for interview support.
  • You would pay for similar services yourself and want one package to coordinate them.
  • The written terms clearly match what you expect from career and visa support.

Run your own break-even comparison

Start with ฿85,000. Add what you would genuinely spend on one month of housing, orientation and any help you expect to use. Then account for what the Standard route includes already. Do not count future income as guaranteed, and do not assign a value to a job placement unless terms and eligibility support that assumption.

Use the cash runway calculator to model your tuition and pre-salary living costs. It cannot price visa services or predict employment.

Questions to get answered in writing

  1. What are the exact accommodation specifications and included dates?
  2. Which nationalities and degree types qualify for guaranteed interviews?
  3. Does placement mean introductions, interviews, an offer or a confirmed start? What refund remedy applies if any?
  4. What support is available after month one and for how long?
  5. What are the deposit, cancellation and course-date-change rules?

Compare current terms with the provider

Fees and package terms can change. Confirm the intake, eligibility and inclusions directly before you make a payment.

content:
Home›Bangkok costs

Budget guide · Updated 1 October 2026

What does a Bangkok TEFL move actually cost?

Start with verified tuition. Add your own housing, daily costs, flight and the months you may need to cover before your first pay arrives.

Affiliate disclosure: SiamTEFL may earn a commission from course referrals. Our budget tool includes no commission or provider price assumptions beyond listed tuition.

Known course fees; unknown personal budget

The provider currently lists Standard at ฿45,000, TQUK Level 5 at ฿50,000, a paid internship at ฿90,000 and All-In at ฿130,000. These are tuition/package prices, not your total cost to relocate and wait for work.

For a Standard or Level 5 student, accommodation and flights are not included. The All-In page lists first-month accommodation, but flights, food, transport and later housing still need a separate budget.

฿45,000Standard, 120-hour course
฿50,000TQUK Level 5, 168 guided hours
฿130,000All-In package, includes month-one accommodation

Source: Essential TEFL current courses and fees, checked 1 October 2026.

Build the full cash runway

For a course-only route, plan for: tuition + flight + accommodation deposit and rent + food + transport + visa/administrative costs + a contingency buffer. Multiply monthly living expenses by the number of months from arrival until you reasonably expect your first salary.

The provider’s Bangkok course FAQ recommends bringing ฿100,000–฿150,000, citing an accommodation deposit, living during the course and expenses while waiting for first pay. Treat this as a provider recommendation—not a personal quote or guaranteed safe amount. Your rent, timing, salary, booking terms and circumstances may differ.

For All-In, subtract the first month’s included accommodation only if the written terms match your stay. Do not assume the course fee includes flight, meals or months after the first.

Costs to research for yourself

  • Accommodation: compare short-term and monthly options near your campus or likely workplace; check deposit and utility terms.
  • Food and transport: estimate from your own habits and commute, not an average that may not fit.
  • Arrival: include flight, baggage, local SIM, airport transfers and any items you need on arrival.
  • Timing gap: course duration does not predict the date you begin work or receive a salary. Include a conservative runway and emergency funds.
  • One-off fees: confirm visa, document, medical, police-check and payment costs applicable to your nationality and situation with the relevant authority/provider.

Estimate your own number

Use your best current quotes and select how many months of living costs you need to cover before first pay. The estimate updates instantly and lets you account for accommodation included in the All-In package for month one.

Open the Thailand cash calculator ↗

Salary is not a guaranteed offset

The provider publishes indicative teacher salary ranges and examples, but roles depend on qualifications, nationality, school requirements, timing and available jobs. Salary figures do not establish a guaranteed job or first-pay date. Avoid borrowing or booking on the assumption that you will start work immediately after the course.

Before paying

  1. Confirm the full course fee, deposit and balance due dates for your intake.
  2. Ask what employment support means for your eligibility profile.
  3. Get housing inclusion and refund/cancellation terms in writing.
  4. Price your own travel and living expenses; keep a separate emergency buffer.

Check the live course details

Verify dates, fees and included items with the provider before booking. Then return to your own budget—not the headline tuition figure—to decide if the timing works.

schema.headline: Online vs In-Person TEFL in Thailand: How to Choose

content:
Home›Course formats

Format comparison · Updated 1 October 2026

Online or in-person TEFL in Thailand?

The better format is the one that fits the training, qualification and experience your target employers ask for—and the life you can realistically organise.

Affiliate disclosure: This page may earn commission from a referred course enrolment. We do not claim that one format is universally superior.

Start with what you need from training

Online and in-person courses differ in delivery, opportunities for observed practice, location requirements and logistics. “Online” is not one consistent standard; compare the syllabus, hours, feedback, assessed teaching practice and awarding body for each individual program.

Essential TEFL’s Bangkok courses are described as in-person and include supervised practice with real students. The current course comparison lists a 120-hour Standard route at ฿45,000 and a 168-guided-hour Level 5 route at ฿50,000. Confirm the exact course and certificate details on the provider’s current pages.

Primary source: Essential TEFL course overview and course comparison, checked 1 October 2026.

Side-by-side decision factors

FactorOnline routeIn-person Bangkok route
Where you studyUsually from home; delivery variesAttend in Bangkok for scheduled training
Observed practiceDepends on provider and course design; inspect syllabusCan include supervised lessons with local learners; verify exact format
FlexibilityOften more self-paced, but deadlines and tutor access varyFixed dates and attendance; cohort and classroom routine
Relocation budgetNo Bangkok move required during trainingInclude travel, accommodation and pre-salary runway
Local contextMay require you to find experience and networks separatelyTraining in Thailand may provide local context and contacts; outcomes vary
Qualification valueDepends on awarding body, hours and assessmentAlso depends on exact certificate; location alone does not guarantee acceptance

An online course may fit if…

  • You cannot relocate or attend fixed weekday classes now.
  • You need flexible pacing around work or family commitments.
  • Your target employers confirm they accept the qualification you are considering.
  • You have a plan for practical classroom experience and feedback if these are important to your goals.

In-person training may fit if…

  • You can be in Bangkok and want a scheduled, intensive cohort.
  • You value observed teaching practice with learners in a local classroom.
  • You want to experience the city and build local connections while training.
  • You have budgeted for the move and the time before any first salary.

Questions to ask any provider

  1. How many guided learning hours and how many face-to-face contact hours?
  2. Will I teach real learners under observation? How many lessons and what feedback?
  3. Which organisation awards the certificate, and can I verify its status?
  4. What do employers in my target location require?
  5. What job support is offered, who is eligible, and what is explicitly not guaranteed?

Considering a Bangkok course?

Read the independent Essential TEFL review and calculate your full cash runway before you compare enrollment fees.

Why this site exists

Independent decisions, made clearer.

SiamTEFL is an independently operated guide for people considering TEFL training and teaching in Thailand.

Our purpose

Course pages explain what providers sell. We help prospective trainees compare the choice, separate a course fee from a relocation budget and spot questions worth resolving before a deposit.

Our independence

SiamTEFL is not the training provider, an accreditation body, immigration adviser or employment agency. We are not affiliated with Essential TEFL beyond a referral relationship. We have not independently audited course delivery, hiring outcomes or student satisfaction.

Some links may earn a commission if a reader enrols. This commercial relationship is disclosed where relevant. It does not alter a reader’s price, and it does not guarantee that we will recommend a course.

Editorial standards

  • Use provider primary sources for current fees and package inclusions, with access dates.
  • Attribute provider claims and distinguish them from independently verified facts.
  • Avoid guarantees about jobs, salaries, visa outcomes or future results.
  • Correct material errors and display the last-reviewed date.

For our source and review process, see Methodology. For commercial relationships, read the affiliate disclosure.

Contact

For corrections, source requests or privacy questions, use the SiamTEFL contact page.

content:
Home›Methodology

Editorial policy

How we research and update this guide.

Our goal is to make evidence and uncertainty visible, especially where a booking decision involves money and relocation.

Sources and verification

Prices and package inclusions are checked against provider primary pages. The review identifies those pages and records the date accessed. Provider pages tell us what the provider currently publishes; they do not independently validate teaching quality, outcomes or commercial terms.

Where provider pages use inconsistent wording, we avoid the strongest interpretation and ask readers to confirm the exact terms in writing. We do not infer fees or included services when a source does not publish them.

Claims and employment

We distinguish among course completion, job-search support, introductions, interviews and employment. These are different outcomes. We do not present salary figures as a promise, claim a job is guaranteed unless contract terms explicitly establish that for a particular eligible reader, or predict visa/work-permit outcomes.

Budgets and calculator

Verified course fees are separated from user-supplied inputs such as accommodation, food, transport, flight and emergency buffer. The calculator is an arithmetic planning aid. It cannot model every fee, validate a personal budget or predict when someone will be employed or paid.

Reviews and corrections

We do not manufacture experience, testimonials, graduate outcomes or star ratings. Please use our contact page with a source, correction or conflict to review. We aim to recheck core fee references periodically and when readers report a material change.

Core official course pages last checked 1 October 2026. Individual pages display their review date.

Commercial relationships

SiamTEFL uses referral links. If a reader enrols after following a referral link, SiamTEFL may receive commission. This site is not the course provider and no provider has editorial control over our independent decision framework. See the full affiliate disclosure.

Commercial transparency

How referral links work here.

Some outbound links may earn SiamTEFL a commission if you enrol after clicking.

Our relationship

SiamTEFL participates in an affiliate referral relationship with Essential TEFL. If you use a SiamTEFL referral link and make a qualifying purchase or enrolment, we may receive a commission from the provider or its affiliate platform. You do not pay more because you used our link.

Affiliate links are labelled with the appropriate relationship attributes in the page markup and accompanied by a disclosure near relevant recommendations or calls to action.

Editorial independence

Compensation does not establish that a course is right for you. Our comparisons consider published course information and decision factors, and describe limitations in support claims. We do not claim to have independently tested or audited the provider. We encourage readers to compare alternatives and request written terms.

Tracking

Optional Google Analytics loads only if you choose “Allow analytics.” With your permission, SiamTEFL records page views and an affiliate_click event with the page path, provider name and CTA placement. We do not send the full referral URL or calculator values to Google. Enhanced Measurement is off, so Google does not automatically collect scroll or outbound-link events through this stream. The provider or affiliate platform may separately collect referral clicks and conversions under its own privacy notice and terms. You can change your choice using “Privacy choices” in the footer.

Do not enter personal or sensitive information into the calculator; values are processed locally in your browser.

Questions

For questions about referral links or this policy, use our contact page.

Home›Privacy

Effective 1 October 2026

Privacy policy

A plain-language summary of data handling on this guide. Optional Google Analytics stays off unless you choose “Allow analytics.” You can change your choice at any time using “Privacy choices” in the footer.

Calculator inputs

The budget calculator runs in your browser. The amounts you enter are not sent to SiamTEFL or stored by this site.

Affiliate links

When you click an affiliate link, your browser visits the third-party provider with a referral code. The provider or affiliate platform may collect information about visits, purchases, device or browser under its own privacy policy. Review those terms directly.

If you allow analytics, Google Analytics receives page-view events and affiliate_click events containing the page path, provider name and CTA placement. We do not send calculator entries, the full referral URL or its referral code as event parameters. Google Analytics may use cookies and collect standard device, browser, approximate location and usage information under Google’s privacy terms. Enhanced Measurement is disabled for this stream. If you decline or later withdraw consent, the Google tag is not loaded on later visits and further event collection is disabled on the current page. You can change your choice using “Privacy choices” in the footer.

Cookies and third parties

SiamTEFL does not load Google Analytics or its analytics cookies unless you allow analytics. The site loads fonts from Google Fonts; your browser may connect to Google to retrieve them. The site also links to external course and information sites, which have their own data practices. See Google’s privacy policy for information about Google Analytics data handling.

Contact

For privacy questions, use the SiamTEFL contact page. Messages sent to the published contact address are used to respond and are not published.

Changes

Material changes to data collection should be reflected in this policy before the new service is enabled. For privacy questions, use the contact options on our Contact page.
